title: How long is the passing ship?
hook: Measure both ends at the same time in your frame.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Length along the direction of motion is L = L₀ / gamma. At 0.6c, gamma = 1.25, so 100 m / 1.25 = 80 m.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Length along the direction of motion is L = L₀ / gamma. At 0.6c, gamma = 1.25, so 100 m / 1.25 = 80 m.

claims.text: Length along the direction of motion is L = L₀ / gamma. At 0.6c, gamma = 1.25, so 100 m / 1.25 = 80 m. Special relativity; the endpoints are measured simultaneously in the observer's inertial frame. Transverse dimensions are unaffected.

recall.question: A 50 m object moves lengthwise at 0.6c. What length is measured in the observer's rest frame?
recall.why: At 0.6c multiply the rest length by 0.8: 50 × 0.8 = 40 m.
